notes: Source: Bears 2026 media guide, 'INDIVIDUAL' section. Career tables are on PDF pages 245-248 (passing/rushing 245-246, receptions 246-247, receiving/sacks 247-248, interceptions 248). Season and game record lists are on pages 253-258 and 263 (RUSHING 253-254, PASSING 255, RECEIVING 256-257, SACKS 258, INTERCEPTIONS BY 263), each printed as LIFETIME / SEASON / GAME groups with the value, player and year or date.

Page 250 repeats the rookie records (same values as the 'ROOKIE ...' blocks on pages 253-257); those rookie blocks, the 'OPPONENT ...' blocks, 'consecutive games' blocks and the postseason pages (277-280) were skipped, as were scoring, kicking, punting, returns and fumbles.

through_season 2025: the lists include 2025 seasons and games (Caleb Williams 3,942 passing yards in 2025, D'Andre Swift 2025, Kevin Byard at Las Vegas 9/28/2025) and the active players' career spans read '2024-present', '2020-present', '2023-present'.

The record-block lists (LIFETIME/SEASON/GAME) print no rank numbers: value groups are listed in order and tied holders are stacked under one printed value. 'rank' here is the competition rank over the named holders (a group of 3 tied for first gets rank 1,1,1 and the next group rank 4), tie is true for every row that shares its value; raw shows a parenthesised value, e.g. '(14) Gale Sayers 1965', where the guide prints the value only once for the group.

The career tables print rank numbers; 'T-4' / 'T-8' / 'T-11' are ties (tie true, rank = the printed number). Two guide numbering quirks kept as printed: career passing prints rank 12 twice (Lujack 6,295 and Bukich 6,254, different values), and career sacks prints 'Otis Wilson' with no rank under '10. Khalil Mack' (both 36.0, treated as tied for 10).

career pass_td, rush_td and rec_td each have a 'list' (the LIFETIME top 3 from the records block) and a 'column' (the TD column of the full career table, printed order = sorted by yards) so ranks 4-5 can be recovered.

season rush_yds uses the ranked '1,000-YARD RUSHING SEASONS' list (page 246) and season rec_yds uses the ranked '1,000-YARD RECEIVERS' list (page 247) because they are longer than the 3-line record blocks; their top 3 agree with the record blocks (Payton 1,852/1,684/1,610; Marshall 1,508, Jeffery 1,421, Robinson 1,400). Likewise the career pass/rush/rec/rec_yds/int tables agree with the LIFETIME blocks on pages 253, 255, 256, 257 and 263.

Sacks: the career list on pages 247-248 is headed 'CAREER SACKS (SINCE 1982)' (official only). The page 258 record block (a second career 'list' for sacks, plus the season and game lists) sits under the banner 'ALL SACK STATISTICS PRIOR TO 1982 ARE UNOFFICIAL (SINCE 1970)', so its lifetime numbers include unofficial 1970-81 sacks (Dan Hampton 82 vs 57.0). Jim Osborne's 4-sack game (9/23/1973) is therefore unofficial.

Guide inconsistencies (values kept as printed): the CAREER RECEPTIONS table gives Cole Kmet 288 catches / 2,939 yards and DJ Moore 244 / 3,012, while the CAREER RECEIVING table gives Kmet 280 / 2,865 and Moore 233 / 2,828; the career passing row for Caleb Williams prints Cmp 661 with Cmp% 60.3 (661/1,130 would be 58.5%; the Annual Passing Leaders page 315 gives 351 + 330 = 681, so 661 is a misprint, while his 7,483 yards equal 3,541 + 3,942); the interceptions rows for Doug Buffone (211 yards with a 16.9 average) and Gary Fencik (484 yards with a 12.8 average, 484/38 = 12.74) do not fit their averages. None of these touches the ranked stat except possibly active players' receptions/yards.

Dates in the record blocks are printed with 4-digit years; 'years' holds the date only, 'raw' holds the printed text with the opponent. Names are as printed ('Matt Forté' in tables, 'Matt Forte' on the page 256 receptions block); position tags such as '(WR)' are dropped from name and kept in raw.

Cross-checks inside the guide: season values for rushing yards/TDs (page 314 Annual Rushing Leaders: Payton 1977 1,852/14, 1979 1,610/14, 1976 13 TD, 1984 1,684, Anderson 1988 12 TD, Casares 1956 12 TD, Sayers 1965 14 TD), passing (page 315: Williams 2025 3,942, Kramer 1995 3,838 with 29 TD, Cutler 2014 3,812 with 28 TD), receiving yards (page 318: Marshall 1,508, Jeffery 1,421, Robinson 1,400) and interceptions (page 319: Carrier 1990 10, Jennings 2012 9) agree with the record lists.

Every row was read from 220-300 dpi crops; the yards-per-carry/catch/return columns and completion percentages of the career tables were checked arithmetically (only the guide inconsistencies listed above did not fit).
Tackles: the guide prints no tackles records for any scope.
